posts.headline: Fifteen straight editions of complete silence from One Nut Barner, and Put it in Ra's league-best 20-8 record with a 1.5 average finish just keeps sitting there daring somebody to say something about it.
posts.detail: A 0.714 win percentage and two straight top-2 finishes is exactly the kind of pedigree that should be talking trash, not going quiet — the Cal Berkeley GPA jokes write themselves but the silence writes an even bigger target.

posts.headline: Sasinci has no more preseason left to hide in — Big Head's 13-15 career record now has to justify a title banner in games that actually count.
posts.detail: A weak-minded champion with an enormous head and a habit of threatening to quit monthly is either about to validate the ring or expose it as a fluke, and Week 1 doesn't care about excuses.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh enters live Week 1 still holding the single worst résumé in Busters Anonymous history, and a new roster doesn't erase a 4-10 season with a dead-last 12th-place finish.
posts.detail: The untalented tenth needed a full offseason to escape the basement and instead shows up with the same name, the same energy, and zero evidence anything changed.

posts.headline: The Clown Show kept the name into real Week 1, and the Alaskan Bull Worm has officially run out of preseason cover for the athlete cosplay.
posts.detail: A 15-13 career record and a best finish of 1st means the talent is technically in there somewhere — but a delusional Packers superfan strutting like a pro needs actual production now that games count.

posts.headline: Thicks is still coasting on last year's #FreeMaxx ring, but a 14-14 career record and a 5.5 average finish means the reigning champs have way more hype than substance walking into Week 1.
posts.detail: One title in two seasons with a worst finish of 8th is a shaky foundation for a crown — Klint's Clipboard needs to actually look like a contender now that the games are live, not just the trophy case.
